page.layout: One page of running text in a single column, with a verse reference and its italic verse set apart in the middle, and a catchword and signature at the foot. No margin notes. Running head at the top with the printed page number 549.

main_text.p: Christi conflictum cum Diabolo in deserto, postquàm baptizatus ex aquis Jordanis exiisset, applicat: causa versionis illi, quod putet vocem reptile significare, & Diabolo applicari, eo quod post deceptum primum hominem divinâ sententiâ in serpente damnatus est, ut in ventre reptaret: quæ longè petita sunt. Qui ὄρνεον [?] vertunt, proprie vultur notari volunt, avis rapax & immunda, atque etiam symbolicè Diabolum innui existimant. Hi per mortem angelum intelligunt, qui morte puniverat Ægyptiorum primogenitos, quem adventui Christi concipiunt præmissum: per immundam & rapacem hanc avem Diabolum subsequentem post adventum Christi, qui reliquias absumeret. Verùm רשף [?] in sacris est pruna ardens, & scintillas hinc emicantes notat, Job. 5: 7. Cant. 8: 6. Psal. 76: 4. Atque ita innuit terram primæ stationis ab exitu Christi, prunis & scintillis petendam, quibus inflammetur, & igne absumente vastetur. Ita concipitur terra illa ut anathemate percutienda, Mal. 4: 6, & judicio divino planè absumenda. Vide ad Deut. 32: 24.
main_text.head: Verf. 6.

p.i: Qui flětit & mensus est terram, vidit & diffilire [?] fecit gentes, ut disjecti sint montes æterni, depressi sint colles seculi, bujus sunt itinera seculi.

page.notes: Doubtful readings: "ὄρνεον" (Greek, accent unclear), "רשף" (Hebrew, niqqud unclear), "diffilire" (possibly dissilire). Small marks at the left margin beside "ardens" and before "§. 1." appear to be printed asterisks or stains; they are not transcribed as notes because they could not be confirmed. Heavy ink show-through and foxing across the page. The "ꝭ" in the running head is uncertain.
